This demonstrates a fundamental limitation of GRPO’s advantage calculation in multi-reward optimization which over-compresses the rich group-wise reward signal. Intuitively, ( 𝟶 , 𝟸 ) \mathtt{(0,2)} should produce a stronger learning signal than ( 𝟶 , 𝟷 ) \mathtt{(0,1)} because a total reward of 2 2 indicates simultaneous satisfaction of two rewards, whereas a reward of 1 1 corresponds to achieving only one. Thus, when the other one rollout only receives zero reward, ( 𝟶 , 𝟸 ) \mathtt{(0,2)} should yield a larger relative advantage than ( 𝟶 , 𝟷 ) \mathtt{(0,1)} . This limitation can also introduce risks of training instability due to inaccurate advantage estimates. As shown in Fig. 5 , the correctness reward score begins to decline after approximately 400 training steps when training with GRPO, indicating a partial training collapse.
